summary: Local analysts and union leaders in Cambodia are praising the government's diplomatic efforts following the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers who were held by the Thai military for 155 days. Geopolitical analyst Thong Mengdavid noted that this release is a sign of Thailand's commitment to easing border tensions and preparing for their upcoming February 2026 elections. The soldiers returned to Cambodia on the morning of December 31, 2025.
title: អ្នកវិភាគ សហជីព និងនាយកសាលាបច្ចេកទេស លើកឡើងថា ការវិលត្រឡប់ របស់វីរកងទ័ពទាំង 18រូប គឺជាជោគជ័យ នៃនយោបាយការទូត របស់រាជរដ្ឋាភិបាលកម្ពុជា ជាមួយប្រទេសថៃ
titleEn: Analysts, Unions, and Technical School Directors claim that the return of the 18 heroic soldiers is a success of the Royal Government of Cambodia's diplomacy with Thailand

summary: Defense Ministry spokesperson Maly Socheata stated that as of 8:00 AM on January 1, the frontline remains calm. Cambodian forces are maintaining high vigilance to protect sovereignty while strictly adhering to the ceasefire signed on December 27, 2025. The ministry also highlighted an agreement to avoid spreading fake news to reduce public tension.
title: ស្ថានភាពជួរមុខ មានសភាពស្ងប់ស្ងាត់ ខណៈកងកម្លាំងកម្ពុជាបន្តតាមដាន និងគោរពបទឈប់បាញ់
titleEn: Frontline situation is quiet as Cambodian forces continue to monitor and respect the ceasefire

summary: 18 Cambodian soldiers, captured in July 2025 and held for five months, arrived in Phnom Penh on Wednesday, December 31, to a hero's welcome. Their release was a key condition of a recent truce brokered to end weeks of heavy fighting that reportedly killed dozens and displaced over a million people. Information Minister Neth Pheaktra confirmed their arrival, while the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) monitored the handover, which had been briefly delayed by Thai accusations of drone violations by Cambodia.
title: Cambodian soldiers freed by Thailand receive hero’s welcome

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet has approved the creation of a specialized task force to manage and organize the restoration of livelihoods and infrastructure damaged during the recent border conflict with Thailand. The Ministry of Interior noted significant damage to public facilities and homes in border provinces.
title: PM okays task force to carry out post-conflict restoration

summary: Local officials in Battambang province have reported the discovery of unexploded ordnance (UXO) and large craters in civilian areas following previous Thai artillery shelling. The damage to homes and infrastructure is complicating the return of displaced residents. Authorities cite these findings as evidence of cross-border attacks on civilian property.
title: Unexploded Ordnance, Craters Found in Battambang After Thai Shelling

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior reported that over 5,000 additional displaced civilians have returned to their homes as the ceasefire holds. This follows the successful repatriation of 18 Cambodian soldiers who were held in Thai custody for 155 days. The ministry emphasized that the situation at the border is stabilizing in accordance with the 3rd Special GBC meeting agreements.
title: ក្រសួងមហាផ្ទៃ ៖ មានជនភៀសសឹកជាង 5ពាន់នាក់ទៀត បានបន្តវិលត្រឡប់ទៅលំនៅឋានវិញ
titleEn: Ministry of Interior: Over 5,000 more displaced people have continued to return home

summary: Dr. Kun Nhem, Minister Attached to the PM, delivered gifts and equipment from PM Hun Manet and his wife to soldiers in Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat. The equipment included solar chargers and 2,000 gas masks. During the ceremony, officials praised the soldiers for their 21 days of 'fierce fighting' against what they described as 'cruel Thai aggression' that damaged homes and ancient temples. While the border is currently quiet due to a ceasefire, troops remain on high alert.
title: អំណោយរបស់សម្តេចបវរធិបតី ហ៊ុន ម៉ាណែត និង លោកជំទាវបណ្ឌិត ត្រូវបានបណ្ឌិត គុណ ញឹម បន្តនាំយកទៅប្រគល់ជូនដល់វីរកងទ័ពជួរមុខ ដែលកំពុងឈរជើងការពារបូរណភាពទឹកដី តាមបណ្តោយព្រំដែនកម្ពុជា-ថៃ
titleEn: Gifts from PM Hun Manet and his wife delivered by Dr. Kun Nhem to front-line troops defending territorial integrity along the Cambodia-Thailand border

summary: Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, spokeswoman for the Ministry of National Defence, stated on January 2 that the border remains calm with no new clashes since December 27. She noted that over 393,600 displaced people remain in safety centers, while 15,600 have recently returned home. Cambodian forces remain on high vigilance.
title: Cambodia to Continue Working with Partners to Secure Peace

summary: The Ministry of Interior reported that as of the evening of January 1, 2026, 103,177 displaced people have returned home. However, 409,186 people remain in temporary shelters. The government attributes the return to the effective implementation of the December 27 ceasefire by both sides.
title: Over 100,000 Displaced People Return Home Following Ceasefire

summary: Reports from Oddar Meanchey and Battambang describe widespread destruction of civilian houses, pagodas, and schools due to what authorities call 'indiscriminate Thai bombardment.' Local governors warn of unexploded ordnance (UXOs) preventing safe return.
title: Border communities must rebuild their homes and livelihoods that were destroyed by Thai forces

summary: Experts suggest the ceasefire effective since Dec 27 and the release of 18 Cambodian soldiers are positive steps, but lasting peace requires sustained diplomatic effort. The border has remained calm since the 21-day conflict ended.
title: Border calm offers opportunity for reconciliation, experts say

summary: The Ministry of Interior reports that despite tensions, over 100,000 displaced people returned home by Jan 1. Crucially, 18 Cambodian soldiers who had been detained by Thailand since July 2025 were released and returned via the Ban Laem checkpoint. However, over 400,000 people remain displaced in temporary shelters.
title: Ceasefire Holds as 100,000 Displaced Cambodians Return, 18 Soldiers Repatriated

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action Centre (CMAC) has launched emergency risk education campaigns to protect civilians returning to areas recently hit by shelling. Officials categorize zones into Red (high risk), Yellow (needs clearing), and White (safe).
title: Cambodia intensifies UXO awareness as displaced families return to border zones

summary: The Ministry of Interior reports 512,263 people remain displaced despite the ceasefire. While 5,192 people returned home recently, infrastructure damage and unexploded ordnance in Banteay Meanchey, Oddar Meanchey, and Preah Vihear keep most from returning.
title: Ceasefire holds, but half a million Cambodians remain displaced four days on

summary: The Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport reported that 101 out of 260 schools in Oddar Meanchey province have resumed operations as of Jan 2, 2026. This is seen as a sign of gradual return to normalcy in the border regions following the ceasefire.
title: ក្រសួងអប់រំ ៖ គិតត្រឹមព្រឹកថ្ងៃទី2 មករា គ្រឹះស្ថានសិក្សា 101 ក្នុងខេត្តឧត្តរមានជ័យ បានបើកដំណើរឡើងវិញ
titleEn: Ministry of Education: As of the morning of January 2, 101 educational institutions in Oddar Meanchey have reopened

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated in a press conference on the morning of Jan 2 that Cambodia does not recognize any border adjustments resulting from the military conflict. He referenced recent Thai military assaults involving tanks and drones as the context for this stance, asserting that territorial integrity must be maintained according to original maps.
title: កម្ពុជា មិនទាន់ទទួលស្គាល់ ការកែប្រែព្រំដែន ណាចេញពីការប្រើកម្លាំងទេ
titleEn: Cambodia does not yet recognize any border changes resulting from the use of force

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal statement on January 3, 2026, accusing the Thai military of continuing to occupy Cambodian land in four provinces (Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey) despite the December 27 ceasefire. The ministry claims Thai forces are destroying civil infrastructure and preventing refugees from returning home, violating the UN Charter and the Geneva Convention.
title: ក្រសួងការបរទេស ៖ ការកាន់កាប់ទឹកដីកម្ពុជា ដោយកងទ័ពថៃ ក្រោយបទឈប់បាញ់ គឺជាការរំលោភយ៉ាងជាក់ច្បាស់
titleEn: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Thai Military Occupation of Cambodian Territory After Ceasefire is a Clear Violation

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement demanding Thai forces immediately cease 'hostile military activities' and withdraw all personnel from areas it claims are inside Cambodia. Locations mentioned include Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey provinces. The report highlights alleged destruction of civilian homes by Thai troops after the ceasefire.
title: កម្ពុជា ទាមទារឱ្យថៃ ដកបុគ្គលិក និងសម្ភារៈយោធាទាំងអស់ ចេញពីទឹកដីកម្ពុជា ទៅកាន់ទីតាំងព្រំប្រទល់ ដែលទទួលស្គាល់ដោយច្បាប់
titleEn: Cambodia demands Thailand withdraw all military personnel and equipment from Cambodian territory to legally recognized border locations

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona stated in a press conference that Cambodia does not recognize any border changes resulting from the use of force. He detailed specific Thai actions during the ceasefire, including placing shipping containers, spreading barbed wire, and planting Thai national flags on Cambodian soil. He urged citizens to trust the government's peaceful and legal resolution efforts.
title: Cambodia: Thailand has spread barbed wire, planted flags, destroyed Cambodian homes – acts that violate Cambodia’s territorial integrity, agreed agreements, UN Charter
titleEn: Cambodia: Thailand has spread barbed wire, planted flags, destroyed Cambodian homes

summary: The Ministry of Information issued a 5-point directive to social media users and journalists to prevent 'fake news' and AI-generated 'deepfakes' that could incite racial discrimination or anger during border negotiations. It orders the public to rely only on official government sources to support diplomatic efforts for a permanent ceasefire.
title: Cambodia Issues Media Guidelines to Ease Border Tensions With Thailand

summary: Official government news agency AKP reports that Thai forces have used excavators to level homes and erected shipping containers and barbed wire in the Boeung Trakuon area of Banteay Meanchey province. Governor Oum Reatrey stated this occupation occurred after the Dec 27 ceasefire, displacing over 6,000 people and destroying 1,365 homes.
title: Cambodia Accuses Thai Military of Breaching Ceasefire, Seizing Border Territory

summary: Footage and images shared by Fresh News show Thai military personnel erecting barbed wire fences, placing metal shipping containers, and hoisting the Thai national flag in Prey Chan village, Banteay Meanchey province. These actions reportedly occurred today, Sunday, January 4, 2026, despite the previous week's ceasefire.
title: VIDEO & PICTURES: Thailand continuing to ‘block off’ Cambodian sovereign territory

summary: HE Chan Ratana, Undersecretary of State and Acting Spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated during a live broadcast that the Thai military is ignoring the ceasefire agreement of December 27, 2025. He alleged that Thai forces continue to occupy territory in four provinces and are destroying civilian infrastructure in areas like Prey Chan and Chouk Chey village.
title: The Royal Government of Cambodia has made the strongest protest against Thailand's violations, including its continued presence and illegal occupation of Cambodian territory

summary: Minister of Information Neth Pheaktra issued a directive on Saturday urging social media users and journalists to use information responsibly. The goal is to prevent the spread of 'fake news' that could hinder diplomatic efforts to resolve the ongoing border conflict with Thailand following the December 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodia issues media guidelines to ease border tensions with Thailand

summary: As of January 5, the 2026 academic year in border provinces is in chaos. Over 1,300 schools remain closed across seven provinces, affecting 322,000 students. In Banteay Meanchey, only 9 out of 321 affected schools have reopened. Many schools were directly targeted or destroyed during the fighting in December.
title: Border conflict disrupts 2026 school year for students

summary: Civilian survivors at Wat Samithi Moni Saphon in Serei Saophoan describe the hardships of life in displacement camps. Many, particularly women and the elderly, express deep fear of returning to their villages in Banteay Meanchey due to reports of continued Thai military presence and destruction of their homes.
title: Plea for peace as thousands of Cambodians remain displaced by border violence

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated in a press conference that Thai soldiers have continued to erect barriers, install barbed wire, and loot property from Cambodian civilians despite the December 27 ceasefire. He described these actions as 'inhumane' and a direct violation of international law and the UN Charter. The government maintains that these unilateral physical markers do not change the legal boundary.
title: Royal Government of Cambodia: Thailand's current actions are an 'internationally illegal act and a violation of the international border line that is unacceptable'

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs informed the international community that between December 7 and 27, 2025, Thai forces launched a pre-planned military offensive across four provinces: Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey. The Ministry claims Thai troops continue to occupy areas deep within Cambodian territory even after the ceasefire, preventing civilians from returning to their homes and violating international humanitarian law.
title: Foreign Ministry: Thai military launched large-scale, systematic operation from Dec 7-27

summary: The Cambodian State Secretariat of Border Affairs announced that Thailand postponed a JBC meeting scheduled for the first week of January in Siem Reap. Cambodia has countered with a Note Verbale proposing a new meeting for the second or third week of January to discuss demarcation and the recent deployment of Thai containers and flags in disputed areas like O Bei Chorn.
title: Special meeting of the Joint Boundary Commission postponed by Thailand for ‘internal procedures’

summary: Local residents in Banteay Meanchey province report that Thai forces have demolished over 400 houses in Chouk Chey village using heavy machinery following the ceasefire. According to Ministry of Defense reports, while over 25,000 displaced persons have returned home, more than 640,000 Cambodians remain in safety camps. Civil society groups are calling for Thailand to be held accountable for the destruction of civilian property.
title: ពលរដ្ឋថាថៃកម្ទេចផ្ទះនៅភូមិជោគជ័យអស់ជាង400ខ្នងនិងពង្រីកឈ្លានពានចូលដីខ្មែរបន្ថែមទៀត
titleEn: Residents say Thailand has demolished more than 400 houses in Chouk Chey village and is expanding its invasion into Cambodian territory

summary: The Thai Second Army Region accused Cambodian forces of firing a mortar round that injured a Thai sergeant in the Chong Bok area of Ubon Ratchathani on the morning of January 6. Cambodian defense officials, however, described the incident as an accident involving a 'pile of garbage' or an operational error, denying any intent to target Thai territory. The report notes that Thailand has not yet provided specific evidence of the mortar's origin while investigation continues.
title: Thailand accuses Cambodia over mortar incident on Thai soil, no evidence presented

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona reaffirmed Cambodia's stance based on Franco-Siamese treaties and historical maps. He stated that Cambodia does not recognize any boundary alterations resulting from Thai military force. The government also proposed a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting for the second or third week of January in Siem Reap to discuss the unauthorized placement of barbed wire, containers, and bunkers by Thai troops on Cambodian soil.
title: Spokesperson: Cambodia Firmly Defends International Border Established by the Indochina–Siam Boundary Commission and Rejects Any Border Changes by Force

summary: Local authorities in Banteay Meanchey report that 80 roads, particularly along National Road 58, were severely damaged by Thai artillery and aerial bombing during the conflict from Dec 7–27, 2025. Districts like Ou Chrou and Thmar Puok are heavily affected, with craters making travel difficult. The report also highlights damage to civilian homes, power grids, and water systems.
title: 80 roads in Banteay Meanchey province affected by invasion war and shelling from Thai soldiers

summary: The Ministry of National Defence issued a press release regarding an explosion at 7:27 AM on January 6 in the Mom Bei (Mom 3) area, Preah Vihear. Cambodia states the explosion came from a 'pile of garbage' while troops were cleaning the area, injuring two Cambodian soldiers. The ministry stressed its commitment to the Dec 27 ceasefire and noted that border coordination teams are communicating to resolve the misunderstanding after Thai accusations of mortar fire.
title: Cambodia Clarifies Border Explosion Incident, Reaffirms Full Commitment to Ceasefire

summary: The spokesperson for the Ministry of Interior has issued a formal denial regarding a report by Khaosod English which claimed Thai naval forces seized a Cambodian weapons cache inside a casino building in the Thmor Da area. The Ministry clarified that the building is actually a Cambodian Border Police post located within sovereign Cambodian territory, not a hidden cache, and condemned the report as misinformation.
title: Ministry of Interior denies Khaosod English report on Thai Navy seizing weapon cache

summary: Cambodia has sent a second Note Verbale to Thailand requesting a Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meeting in Siem Reap during the 2nd or 3rd week of January. This follows a postponement by Thailand of a previous request for a meeting in early January. Cambodia aims to discuss demarcation and address ongoing issues of Thai military presence in areas claimed by Cambodia.
title: Cambodia re-proposes to Thailand to convene meeting on border demarcation

summary: Cambodian government spokespeople and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs have highlighted specific border zones where Thai military forces are allegedly operating illegally. The government maintains that any barriers or flags placed by Thai forces do not represent the actual international border and demands a full withdrawal to positions recognized by international law and historical maps. This messaging reinforces the domestic narrative of defending sovereignty against Thai 'encroachment'.
title: ព័ត៌មានអន្តរជាតិសំខាន់ៗប្រចាំថ្ងៃ 06/01/2026
titleEn: Main International News of the Day 06/01/2026

summary: Thai authorities accused Cambodian forces of violating a 10-day-old ceasefire on Tuesday morning after mortar rounds were fired into Ubon Ratchathani province. One Thai soldier was wounded by shrapnel and evacuated for medical treatment. The Cambodian side later claimed the fire was an 'operational error' caused by personnel cleaning a garbage pile. Thailand has lodged a formal protest but emphasized it exercised 'utmost restraint' by not retaliating in kind.
title: Thailand says Cambodia border strike wounds soldier and violates truce

summary: The Cambodian Human Rights Committee (CHRC) has formally filed a complaint to the United Nations regarding the Thai military's occupation and destruction of private property belonging to Cambodian citizens. The complaint alleges that Thai forces have demolished over 400 houses and established military positions in areas recognized as Cambodian territory, specifically in Banteay Meanchey province. Cambodia demands the immediate withdrawal of Thai troops and compensation for affected civilians.
title: Cambodia files complaint to United Nations demanding action against Thai military's occupation of private property

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Interior issued a formal rejection of a news report by Khaosod English claiming Thai Marines found a large arms cache at a casino in Thmor Da. The ministry labeled the report as false and potentially damaging to the fragile peace along the border.
title: Interior Ministry rejects false Thai reports alleging Thai Marines seized ‘large Cambodian arms cache hidden in Casino’

summary: Reports indicate a new border incident in Preah Vihear province. Cambodian officials claim two soldiers were injured by an accidental explosion in a garbage pile. Conversely, Thai media and military sources claim a Thai soldier was wounded by shrapnel from a mortar round fired from the Cambodian side. This marks the first significant tension reported since the December 27 ceasefire.
title: Two Cambodian and one Thai soldiers injured in Mom 3 area by shelling

summary: Two Cambodian soldiers were injured, one severely, following an explosion in Preah Vihear province on Tuesday morning. While Thailand accused Cambodia of a ceasefire violation via mortar fire, Cambodian defense officials characterized the event as an 'operational error' or accident involving a 'pile of garbage' exploding. The Ministry of Defense stated that border coordination teams from both sides are communicating to prevent further escalation.
title: Defence officials say explosion in Preah Vihear province injures two soldiers

summary: The Royal Government of Cambodia outlined a five-point strategy to protect territorial integrity. Minister Prak Sokhonn expressed 'grave concern' over alleged Thai military incursions in Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey provinces, stating that international borders cannot be altered by force.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Sovereignty Stance Amid Border Tensions

summary: A mortar incident on January 3, 2026, in Boeung Trakoun village, Banteay Meanchey, injured one Thai soldier and threatened a fragile 10-day ceasefire. Thailand accused Cambodia of an 'operational error' while China and the US moved to mediate. China is reportedly preparing to host peace talks in Yunnan/Shanghai between the two nations following weeks of deadly clashes and mass civilian displacement.
title: Thailand-Cambodia Border Tensions Increase After Shooting

summary: Cambodian officials have voiced deep concern over the Thai military's installation of barbed wire and shipping containers to block access to Chork Chey village in Banteay Meanchey. Reports indicate similar encroachments in Pursat, Preah Vihear, and Oddar Meanchey, which Cambodia views as a violation of the ceasefire and its sovereignty.
title: Cambodia raises alarm over renewed Thai encroachments

summary: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul stated that the border situation is calm and under control following a New Year de-escalation period. He addressed long-term maritime disputes, rejecting a '50:50' split over overlapping claims and insisting on verifiable international principles. He also confirmed that regional commanders on both sides had exchanged apologies regarding the January 6 mortar incident, effectively settling the matter at the local level.
title: Anutin rejects 50:50 split in maritime talks with Cambodia

summary: The United States committed $45 million to support stabilization efforts following the December 27 ceasefire. Michael George DeSombre, US Assistant Secretary of State, announced the package including $15 million for border stabilization and displaced persons, $10 million for demining, and $20 million to combat cross-border crimes like fraud and drug trafficking. The US welcomed Thailand's release of 18 Cambodian soldiers as a critical trust-building step.
title: US Pledges $45M for Thailand-Cambodia Border Stability

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Sun Chanthol has called on both sides to 'lower the temperature' to protect the ceasefire reached in December. This appeal follows reports of Thai troops plundering Khmer property and installing barriers inside Cambodian territory. The government emphasizes restraint and dialogue to avoid a return to full-scale fighting.
title: Cambodia urges calm to protect fragile ceasefire in Thai border conflict

summary: The Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training announced that 83,685 job vacancies are available across Cambodia for citizens and specifically for the over 300,000 workers who have returned from Thailand due to the border conflict. Most jobs are in agriculture, industry, and services, particularly in Phnom Penh, Kampong Speu, and Kandal.
title: Over 80,000 job opportunities waiting for former workers returning from Thailand

summary: Senate First Vice-President Ouch Borith visited displaced families in Kampong Cham to deliver aid and a message of trust. He urged the public to support the government's leadership in defending national sovereignty while pursuing a peaceful resolution to the border dispute with Thailand. This comes amid reports of Thai military aggression and the displacement of over 500,000 people.
title: Cambodian Senate leader urges public trust in government’s border defence strategy

summary: Royal Government Spokesperson Pen Bona stated that 470,000 out of 640,000 displaced people have returned to their homes as of Friday. 975 schools in the border provinces of Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey, and Pursat have reopened. However, some areas remain inaccessible to civilians due to ongoing Thai military presence and damage to infrastructure.
title: Cambodia Says It Is Strictly Observing Ceasefire, Urges Respect for International Law

summary: PM Hun Manet met with US Assistant Secretary Michael DeSombre, who confirmed that President Donald Trump is monitoring the border situation. The US announced $25 million in assistance: $15 million for border refugees and $10 million for humanitarian demining efforts to clear unexploded ordnance from the conflict.
title: Hun Manet, US Envoy Discuss Cambodia–Thailand Border

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet issued a special statement reaffirming Cambodia's commitment to solving the border conflict through peaceful means and international law. He praised the national solidarity of the Cambodian people and thanked donors for providing essential supplies to frontline soldiers and displaced citizens during the 21-day conflict in December.
title: Cambodia Reaffirms Peaceful, Law-Based Approach to Border Issue

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet reaffirmed that the government is committed to resolving the border dispute with Thailand through technical principles and international law. He highlighted Cambodia's adherence to bilateral treaties and thanked the public for donations to support frontline soldiers and police during the ongoing tensions.
title: Cambodia vows peaceful, law-based resolution to border issue

summary: Four Cambodian fishermen who were recently detained by the Thai Navy have been released and returned to Koh Kong province on the afternoon of January 11. Governor Mithona Phouthong welcomed them back, describing their return as a result of quiet but active diplomatic efforts.
title: Four fishermen arrested by Thailand have returned to Cambodia

summary: As of January 8, over 173,000 Cambodians remain in displacement sites or with host communities. While 71% of those who fled during the peak of the December fighting have returned home, many face destroyed housing and unexploded ordnance (UXO). Significant populations are still concentrated in Siem Reap and Banteay Meanchey provinces requiring food and health assistance.
title: World Vision: 173,000 remain displaced following border conflict

summary: PM Hun Manet announced that the government will use national funds and aid from partners like China and the US to rebuild infrastructure destroyed by the conflict. A task force is studying how to quickly repair schools, health centers, and the O'Chik bridge, which was reportedly destroyed by Thai airstrikes. Around 490,000 of the 640,000 displaced persons have returned home, but over 150,000 remain in camps.
title: Government will restore public infrastructure damaged by Cambodia-Thailand border conflict

summary: Cambodia has officially withdrawn its athletes from the 13th ASEAN Para Games scheduled to be held in Thailand later this month. The decision, cited as being due to safety concerns for athletes and their families, follows a similar withdrawal from the SEA Games in December amid the border conflict that killed 31 civilians and injured 91 others.
title: Cambodia Pulls Para-Athletes From ASEAN Games Over Safety Fears

summary: Political observers, including the Cambodia Watchdog Council, criticized PM Hun Manet for softening his language by calling the recent fighting a 'border dispute' instead of an 'invasion.' They argue that since Thai troops still occupy 14 locations across four provinces and conducted deep airstrikes, the term invasion is legally and factually accurate. Critics worry this change in tone might weaken Cambodia's legal position.
title: Observers criticise Hun Manet for dropping term 'Thai invasion of Cambodia'

summary: Education Minister Hang Chuon Naron announced the creation of a support fund for teachers whose homes were damaged or occupied by Thai forces. As of January 8, 113 schools remain closed across Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, and Banteay Meanchey. Temporary classrooms are being established in displacement camps to ensure continued learning.
title: Ministry of Education ensures displaced students receive education in safe camps

summary: Heng Ratana, Director General of CMAC, presented evidence of Thai artillery and aerial bombings at Preah Vihear Temple. He described the attacks as an aggressive violation of Cambodian sovereignty and a destruction of world heritage, stating that Thailand must take responsibility for the damage caused during the conflict from December 7 to 27, 2025.
title: CMAC shows remnants of Thai bombs at Preah Vihear Temple

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona reported that ministries are 'working hard' to assist war refugees currently in camps along the border. The focus is on providing immediate aid and managing the safe return of citizens to their villages following the recent ceasefire agreement.
title: The Royal Government is working hard to help war refugees
